headline: Multi-omics integration nominates candidate biomarkers and mechanisms in diverse diseases
label: Integrative Transcriptomic Biomarker Discovery
summary: Bulk and single-cell transcriptomes are combined with machine learning and Mendelian randomization to prioritize candidate genes for experimental follow-up.
synthesis: The dominant thread is gene-level prioritization from transcriptomic data, with bulk and single-cell RNA-seq combined with machine learning, Mendelian randomization, WGCNA, or deconvolution to nominate candidate biomarkers in cancer, diabetic kidney disease, keratoconus, psoriasis, and painful diabetic neuropathy. Several items carry this toward mechanism: CTH downregulation in diabetic kidney disease, GM2A linked to keratinocyte inflammation, matCAF differentiation driven by TGF-β1-RUNX2 in bladder cancer, and CLSPN with functional validation in colorectal cancer. Other items extend the approach to histone lactylation in colorectal liver metastasis and circFOXK2-MLL1 H3K4 methylation in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma. What is new is the movement of transcriptome-derived candidates into functional and spatial follow-up, though most links remain associative and several items, such as the butyrate-treated lymphoblastoid RNA-seq, remain descriptive.
